comments.author: @mattmerkel5744
comments.text: It never was “Alabama’s coast.” As you noted. the Spanish possession of Florida extended along the Gulf coast all the way to the Mississippi River. After the British acquired it they split the territory between East Florida and West Florida, which included Mobile Bay, the coastal regions of both present-day Alabama and Mississippi, and parts of present-day Louisiana, which are still referred to as the Florida parishes to this day. There’s a complicated history of wars and treaties (and the Louisiana Purchase) that saw Spanish West Florida partitioned and traded between Britain, Spain and the U.S. — it was even briefly an independent republic. When it was finally acquired by the U.S. it was incorporated into the newly created states of Alabama and Mississippi. Florida’s panhandle east of the Perdido River was never a part of Alabama, although Alabama tried unsuccessfully to buy it from Florida.
